comment: The statement that inadequate funding, inequity, and overuse are the ways shared public infrastructure “most characteristically fails” is broad and potentially unsupported. Failures may also arise from weak adoption, poor data quality, security incidents, unclear accountability, supplier lock-in, or political instability.

public.text: The statement that inadequate funding, inequity, and overuse are the ways shared public infrastructure “most characteristically fails” is broad and potentially unsupported. Failures may also arise from weak adoption, poor data quality, security incidents, unclear accountability, supplier lock-in, or political instability.
public.suggestedRevision: Reframe these as three important failure modes rather than the characteristic failure modes. Add adoption, data quality, security, institutional ownership, interoperability, and supplier dependency to the risk framework.
